title: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t
lede: Ahead of Nvidia's third-quarter results, TechCrunch lists what interim CEO Colette Kress should address: Jensen Huang's future, chip diversion to China and the company's AI deal-making.

points: Huang resigned after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at customer Megaspeed alleged to be a Chinese spy.
A petition with 180,000 signatures asks the board to bring him back; CNBC reports there are no talks to do so.
Megaspeed is accused of diverting restricted chips to China; Nvidia now says it stopped supplying it in June 2025.
Nvidia switched to reporting revenue by customer headquarters rather than shipping address, which hid Singapore's share.
Kress reportedly resisted Huang's biggest AI deals and may take a more cautious line on financing the build-out.

sections.text: Any shift in Nvidia's China policy or its appetite for financing deals feeds straight into GPU supply and the funding behind many AI data centers.
